notes.1: The need to think carefully before answering was illustrated by this question. Almost a third of the candidates suggested that a root hair cell has chloroplasts. Some of these candidates would, having given the question a little more time, have come to the correct conclusion.
notes.6: This was one of the easiest questions on the paper, but that does not detract from the fact that an important topic on the syllabus was thoroughly understood by a very high percentage of the candidates.
notes.9: It was revealing that over a quarter of the candidates confused the names for the canine and incisor teeth. This is a simple recall question and the results highlight a possible area for improved teaching.
notes.12: The comment made with reference to Question 9 also applies here, as well over a quarter of candidates were uncertain of the correct sequence of the parts of the alimentary canal.
notes.25: This proved to be this most demanding question on the paper, and prompted a degree of guess-work. This appeared to reveal two areas of confusion in almost two-thirds of the candidates. First, they were not clear exactly what is carried in the blood, and second, collectively they believed that either cellulose, starch or glycogen are soluble. Significantly, it was only the more able candidates that successfully assimilated the information to reach the correct answer.
notes.30: A third of candidates opted incorrectly for C. This suggests that a large proportion of candidates did not fully understand where mitosis occurs but they could recognise an example of development.
notes.37: It is essential in questions where information is provided in tables or graphs to read the data carefully and decide exactly what facts are being supplied. A third of the candidates opted incorrectly for C. More careful thought was needed to realise that it was the pesticide that was in the lowest concentration which was the most dangerous.
notes.general_comments: The test spread the candidates extremely successfully across the mark range. At the lower end of ability, a larger number of candidates scored less than the total that might have been obtained using the ‘guessing method’. This suggests that several of the questions examined areas where there are traditional misconceptions.
